# 4-Day Paris Itinerary for 2 Adults

A moderate-pace Paris plan with one hotel base, museum time, scenic walking, one nice dinner, and one dedicated shopping half-day. I’m assuming mid-range 3–4 star lodging, mostly metro/taxis as needed, and no flights in the budget.

## Paris Plan by Day and Time Block

### Day 1: Arrival + Left Bank Stroll
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and take it easy with coffee near your hotel.
- Afternoon: Walk the Seine from Saint-Germain to Île de la Cité; keep this light to recover from travel.
- Evening: Early dinner in Saint-Germain-des-Prés, then a short riverside walk.

### Day 2: Louvre + Tuileries + Elegant Dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Louvre Museum, focusing on a few wings rather than trying to see everything.
- Afternoon: Tuileries Garden, Place de la Concorde, and a relaxed walk toward the Opéra area.
- Evening: Your nice dinner night — book a classic French restaurant in the 1st or 8th arrondissement.

### Day 3: Musée d’Orsay + Saint-Germain + Shopping Block
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Musée d’Orsay for impressionist and 19th-century art.
- Afternoon: Dedicated shopping block in Le Marais or around Boulevard Haussmann/Galeries Lafayette.
- Evening: Casual dinner near your hotel or in Le Marais, then a low-key neighborhood walk.

### Day 4: Montmartre + Final Museum or Flexible Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Montmartre walk, including Sacré-Cœur and nearby streets.
- Afternoon: Choose one smaller museum or use the time for café stops, souvenirs, and packing.
- Evening: Final dinner close to your hotel, then depart or overnight depending on your schedule.

## Neighborhoods to Stay In

| Neighborhood | Best For | Trade-off | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Saint-Germain-des-Prés | Walkability, cafés, central location | Higher prices | Excellent |
| Le Marais | Shopping, dining, lively streets | Can be busy at night | Excellent |
| 1st Arrondissement | Closest to major sights | Often expensive, less local feel | Very good |
| 7th Arrondissement | Quiet, elegant, good for museums | Less nightlife | Very good |
| 9th Arrondissement | Good value, shopping access | Slightly less scenic | Good |

### Best fit for your trip
- **Top pick: Saint-Germain-des-Prés** for a balanced, classy base with easy walking and metro access.
- **Best for shopping lovers: Le Marais** if you want stylish streets and easy access to boutiques.
- **Best quieter option: 7th Arrondissement** if you prefer a calmer stay near major museums.

## Rough Spending Breakdown for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimate | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel, 3 nights | €750–€1,050 | Mid-range central hotel, one room |
| Meals + drinks | €350–€500 | Includes one nice dinner |
| Museums + entry fees | €80–€140 | Louvre, Orsay, possible extra museum |
| Local transport | €40–€80 | Metro, occasional taxi |
| Shopping block | €150–€300 | Flexible, depends on purchases |
| Buffer | €80–€180 | Snacks, coffee, small extras |
| Total | **€1,450–€2,250** | Targeting the lower-middle range keeps you near budget |

### Budget fit
- To stay near **€1,800**, aim for a hotel around **€800–€900 total** for 3 nights.
- Keep taxis limited and choose **one premium dinner** instead of multiple upscale meals.
- Shopping is the easiest variable to trim if you want more comfort elsewhere.

## Quick Actions
